name: precision before anything else
verdict: RECORDED - constrains claims, does not fail the study
source: results/pcrl_nonlinear_rank_v1/PAIRED_INTERVALS.csv (2018 development pools, paired-household bootstrap, same four sensitive endpoints, 5 comparison families)
question: With an adjusted one-sided bound estimate + z*SE, is a .001-nat margin demonstrable at this sample size?
conclusion: For the historical comparisons on the 2018 development pools, precision is limited NEAR EQUALITY: an adjusted one-sided upper bound at or below .001 was not achievable for a comparison whose point estimate sat near zero (smallest adjusted half-width 0.00220 nats, medians 0.0069-0.0136; already true unadjusted at one-sided 95 percent, smallest 0.00141). This is a statement about those comparisons and that regime, not about the reachability of the operating point and not about any mechanism achievable precision.
A .001 point-estimate SCREEN remains runnable and is what the predecessor used.
More fitted channels, release draws or optimizer seeds do not supply more independent households; bootstrap units are households.
A negative estimate is the route to a pass: a candidate must REDUCE measured additional sensitive recovery relative to same-host J.
consequences_for_this_study: Candidate-specific intervals are computed and reported wherever prescribed, never withheld because historical precision was poor.
The .001 margin and every other scientific criterion are unchanged.
Registered prediction P8 stands CONFIRMED in its literal form; the generalization to any mechanism is withdrawn in AMENDMENT_1.md.

amendment.gate_status: unchanged: registered as constraining claims only, never an operational stopping gate
amendment.effect: conclusion narrowed to limited precision near equality for the historical comparisons
why: The gate is one-sided (estimate + z*SE <= .001), so a sufficiently negative estimate passes at any observed half-width; the original conclusion implicitly assumed the estimate was near zero.
Historical half-widths do not lower-bound a new mechanism paired-loss SE, which is a property of the specific pair compared, not of the pool.
amendment.narrowed_conclusion: For the historical comparisons on the 2018 development pools, precision is limited NEAR EQUALITY: an adjusted one-sided upper bound at or below .001 was not achievable for a comparison whose point estimate sat near zero (smallest adjusted half-width 0.00220 nats, medians 0.0069-0.0136; already true unadjusted at one-sided 95 percent, smallest 0.00141). This is a statement about those comparisons and that regime, not about the reachability of the operating point and not about any mechanism achievable precision.

conclusion: Every sensitive endpoint has an adjusted one-sided half-width above .001 nats; the fraction is 1.00.
The best case across all endpoints and families is 0.00220 nats adjusted, 0.00141 unadjusted at one-sided 95%.

Therefore a .001-nat CONFIRMATION claim is not demonstrable at this sample size even with a point estimate of exactly zero, on any endpoint, under any weighting, and the multiplicity adjustment is not what causes this: it already fails unadjusted.
A .001 point-estimate SCREEN remains runnable and is what the predecessor used; the limit is on confidence statements, not on development screening.
More fitted channels do not supply more independent households. This is a property of the evidence base, not of any mechanism.
consequences_for_this_study: No stage of this study may make a confirmation claim at .001 on any endpoint.
The budget ladder is set from this gate, in advance, not relaxed later after an outcome.
Registered prediction P8 is CONFIRMED, and more strongly than stated: it predicted at least one endpoint would fail, and all of them do.
